title: Why You Will (Probably) Lose Money Trading Options
summary: Survey of academic research showing retail options traders lose billions, pay huge spreads, trade for gambling motives, and are targeted by brokerages.

assertions.quote: most investors take significant losses on their options trade trades much larger than the losses they take from Equity trading

verdicts.note: Studies by Bauer et al., Bryzgalova et al. and de Silva et al. find retail options trading loses money in aggregate and per trade.

Retail (wholesaler-executed) options trades lost $1.14bn in aggregate over Nov 2019-Jun 2021 at a 10-day horizon, before $4.13bn of spread costs, concentrated in sub-week at-the-money calls; measured in aggregate, not per trade, and not compared with stock trades.

assertions.quote: this suggests that gambling and sensation seeking rather than hedging are why people are trading options

verdicts.note: Dutch broker data and US exchange data show retail option positions are not hedges and concentrate in short-dated out-of-the-money calls.
Retail options trades are 69% calls, mostly at-the-money or slightly out-of-the-money, half in sub-week expiries, patterns the authors read as speculation rather than hedging.

assertions.quote: a 12.6% or 29% bid ask spread is a very high transaction cost to overcome

verdicts.note: Average quoted bid-ask spread of S&P 500 stock options is 17.2% versus 3.55 bps for the stocks; retail's preferred sub-week options carry a 12.3% spread and PFOF for options is about double that for stocks.

assertions.quote: they overpay for options relative to realized volatility they incur enormous bid ask spreads and they sluggishly respond to announcements

verdicts.note: de Silva, Smith and So document retail losses of five to fourteen percent around earnings announcements from overpaying for implied volatility.

assertions.quote: retail options trading is profitable for the brokerages facilitating it

verdicts.note: SEC filings show options order-flow payments per contract far exceed those for equities, giving zero-commission brokers a direct incentive.

Wholesalers pay brokerages for order flow, giving brokers an incentive to encourage more trading in wider-spread assets; in Q2 2021 PFOF was $581m for options versus $284m for stocks, and options are prominent on gamified apps.

assertions.quote: Traders exposed to their top performing peers tend to take more risk trade more overall and be less satisfied with their own results

verdicts.note: An experimental study found this effect and social-trading platform data point the same way, though effect sizes vary.

assertions.quote: retail trades in complex options return netive 16.4% over 3 days on average with losses increasing with complexity

verdicts.note: One 2023 study finds this; the result is recent and not yet widely replicated.

assertions.quote: retail investors do not have the same resources information or knowledge as institutions and they're more prone to behavioral biases
one of the best places for institutions to profit off of retail investors

verdicts.note: Exchange and wholesaler data show market makers are the counterparty capturing retail option losses and spreads.
Indirect costs of $4.13bn paid by retail option traders through effective spreads become revenue for market makers and exchanges, five times direct commissions and three times the raw trading loss.

assertions.quote: successful Traders post their wins for everyone to see making it seem possible for everyone else watching
it's a long and boring process that consists of saving and investing in a diversified lowcost portfolio
